newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strauss-Kahn not opposed to Fr Telecom sale-source.
newsitem.headline: Strauss-Kahn not opposed to Fr Telecom sale-source.

text.p: French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn does not oppose opening up France Telecom's capital under certain conditions but no decision has been taken, a government source said on Thursday.

The source confirmed comments by Strauss-Kahn earlier in the week to a closed-door meeting of Socialist parliamentarians in which the minister said, "Personally, I'm not against the opening of the capital on condition that the promises of the prime minister be taken into account."
But both Strauss-Kahn and Christian Pierret, secretary of state for industry, had made comments favouring such a move, the source noted.
On Thursday, French daily Liberation quoted Christian Pierret in an interview as saying at least part of the capital of France Telecom might be opened up.

"With the finance minister, we fixed three aims -- to reinforce France Telecom's strength as a big European telecoms operator, guarantee its independence and allow it to attain critical mass on a world scale".
"All this," Pierret said, "implies at least a minimum opening to the world of (financial) markets."

Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin said during the election campaign that he wanted to consult France Telecom staff before deciding whether to proceed with the sale of a minority stake in the telecoms operator.

The previous conservative government had planned to launch the sale in early June of 30 to 35 percent of France Telecom in what would have been possibly the biggest French stock market operation ever.
The Socialists pledged during the campaign to put privatisations on hold and the source said there were "many political considerations" attached to the France Telecom decision.
